paragraphs: Rav Hanina of Sura on the Euphrates.

Bava Metzia 61b relates that Ravina visited Sura on the Euphrates; Hyman cites Rashi's explanation that this is not ordinary Sura. Rav Chanina of Sura on the Euphrates asks Ravina why the Exodus is mentioned in the law of creeping creatures, etc. Seder Ha Dorot conjectures Rav Chaviva of Sura on the Euphrates. Hyman comments, “A sage is preferable to a prophet,” reporting that this reading occurs in the source supplied as ברק״ם and in Sheiltot, Vaera.

notes.text: The supporting-source siglum ברק״ם remains unresolved. Hyman’s sage-better-than-prophet comment celebrates the apparent confirmation of Seder HaDorot’s conjecture; it is not a new identification made here.

The saved whole Davidson Bava Metzia 61b scalar has Ravina visiting Sura de Perat and full Rav Chanina asking HIM about the Exodus in the creeping-creatures rule. It confirms the question's direction and full local Rav title, not Chaviva in the other cited witnesses. Rashi's geographical gloss, Seder Ha Dorot's conjecture and the supporting-witness report remain Hyman's attributions. ברק״ם, older machine בדק״ם, may intend Dikdukei Soferim but repeated errors elsewhere do not prove that expansion or print history. The sage-preferable-to-prophet remark celebrates Hyman's reported support, not an independently admitted identity.

The consulted scan of Hyman, volume II, printed p. 499, retains Chanina, the proposed Chaviva reading, the sage-and-prophet remark, and the supporting-source reports. Davidson Bava Metzia 61b directly has Chanina asking Ravina the question, while the directly consulted Rashi gloss says that Sura on the Euphrates is not ordinary Sura. These witnesses support the local passage and Rashi’s distinction; they do not independently establish the Chaviva reading in the other works. The supplied ברק״ם remains unexpanded: neither inspection of Hyman’s abbreviated source label nor comparison with older OCR is a collation of the work he cited. The exact Seder HaDorot, variants-work and Sheiltot passages remain uncollated here. Hyman’s apparent confirmation of the conjecture is preserved as his argument, without an identity merger.
